## How Owners Are Created in the PetClinic Spring Boot Project

This is a Spring PetClinic REST project. Owner creation flows through one endpoint: `POST /api/owners` (operationId `addOwner`), handled by `OwnerRestControllerV1`. The API is OpenAPI-generated (controllers implement generated interfaces; DTOs are generated from `openapi.yml`).

### 1. Owner entity class
`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/model/Owner.java`

- `@Entity @Table(name = "owners")`, extends `Person` (which supplies `firstName`/`lastName`).
- Fields: `address` (`@NotEmpty`), `city` (`@NotEmpty`), `telephone` (`@NotEmpty`, `@Pattern` E.164 `^\+[0-9]{8,15}$`), `email` (`@Email`), and a `Set<Pet> pets`.
- `registrationDate`:
```java
@Column(name = "registration_date", columnDefinition = "DATE")
private LocalDate registrationDate;   // getter/setter at lines 106-112
```
- Extra derived fields set during creation: `customerCode`, `householdId`, `namesakeCount`, `membershipNumber` (all plain `String`/`Integer` columns).
- DB schema confirms `registration_date DATE` (e.g. `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/resources/db/h2/schema.sql:39`, plus hsqldb/mysql/postgres variants).

### 2. OwnerRepository interface
`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/repository/OwnerRepository.java`

Plain (non-Spring-Data) interface. Methods:
- `Collection<Owner> findByLastName(String lastName)`
- `Page<Owner> findByLastName(String lastName, Pageable pageable)`
- `Owner findById(int id)`
- `void save(Owner owner)`
- `Collection<Owner> findAll()`
- `Page<Owner> findAll(Pageable pageable)`
- `void delete(Owner owner)`

All throw `DataAccessException`. Implementations: `springdatajpa/SpringDataOwnerRepository.java`, `jpa/JpaOwnerRepositoryImpl.java`, `jdbc/JdbcOwnerRepositoryImpl.java`.

### 3. Controller/service handling owner creation (POST)
Controller: `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/controller/v1/OwnerRestControllerV1.java`
(V2 controller `.../v2/OwnerRestControllerV2.java` only does paginated *listing*, no create.)

Signature (implements generated `OwnersApi`):
```java
@PreAuthorize("hasRole(@roles.OWNER_ADMIN)")
@Override
public ResponseEntity<OwnerDto> addOwner(OwnerFieldsDto ownerFieldsDto)   // lines 121-185
```

Creation logic, in order:
1. Maps DTO to `Owner` via `ownerMapper.toOwner(...)`.
2. Defaults `registrationDate` to `LocalDate.now()` if null (lines 126-128).
3. Normalizes address via `AddressNormalizer`; blank -> `400 BAD_REQUEST` (lines 129-133).
4. Normalizes telephone via `TelephoneNormalizer`; null (invalid E.164) -> `400 BAD_REQUEST` (lines 134-138).
5. If email present, trims and validates against `EMAIL_PATTERN`; invalid -> `400 BAD_REQUEST`; else stores lower-cased (lines 139-146).
6. Duplicate telephone across all owners -> `409 CONFLICT` (lines 147-154).
7. `>= 50` owners already in same normalized city -> `409 CONFLICT` (lines 155-161).
8. Household duplicate (same normalized lastName + address) unless `sharesHousehold=true` -> `409 CONFLICT` (lines 162-171).
9. Derives and sets `householdId`, `customerCode` (`nextCustomerCode`), `namesakeCount`, `membershipNumber` (lines 172-179; helper methods lines 192-247).
10. `clinicService.saveOwner(owner)`, builds `Location` header, returns `201 CREATED` with `OwnerDto` (lines 180-184).

Service passthrough: `ClinicServiceImpl.saveOwner` (line 234) -> `ownerRepository.save(owner)`. Interface at `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/service/ClinicService.java:59`.

Helper collaborators (both `@Component`):
- `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/controller/TelephoneNormalizer.java` (E.164, default country code `+61`; returns `null` when unnormalizable).
- `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/controller/AddressNormalizer.java` (trim/collapse/upper-case/expand abbreviations; blank -> "").

OpenAPI request schema `OwnerFields` (`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/resources/openapi.yml:1991-2070`) enforces bean-validation constraints before the controller runs: `firstName`/`lastName` letters-only patterns, `address`/`city` non-blank patterns, telephone length, email format, optional `registrationDate` (date), and write-only `sharesHousehold`. The `POST /owners` operation (lines 65-97) declares responses `201`, `400`, `500` only.

### 4. How errors/rejections are returned as HTTP responses
Two distinct patterns are in use:

A. In-controller `ResponseEntity` with bare status (used by `addOwner` for business-rule rejects):
```java
return new ResponseEntity<>(HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST);   // blank address, bad phone, bad email
return new ResponseEntity<>(HttpStatus.CONFLICT);       // dup phone, city cap, household dup
```
No response body for these; also `HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND` for missing owners in `getOwner`/`updateOwner`/`deleteOwner`.

B. Global exception handler producing RFC-7807 `ProblemDetail` bodies:
`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/advice/ExceptionControllerAdvice.java` (`@ControllerAdvice`)
- `handleGeneralException(Exception)` -> `500`.
- `handleDataIntegrityViolationException(DataIntegrityViolationException)` -> `404`.
- `handleMethodArgumentNotValidException(MethodArgumentNotValidException)` -> `400`, attaching `schemaValidationErrors` (list of `ValidationMessageDto`) and an `errors` array of rejected field names. This is what catches bean-validation failures from the OpenAPI-declared `OwnerFields` constraints.
- `handleAccessDeniedException` re-throws so Spring Security yields `403`.
- Helper `detailBuild(...)` builds `ProblemDetail` with type/title/detail/timestamp.

A separate helper `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/controller/BindingErrorsResponse.java` can serialize field errors to JSON, but note `addOwner` does not use it — it returns bare status codes. No `ResponseStatusException` and no custom exception classes are used anywhere.

### 5. Existing tests for owner creation
Only three test files exist, all under `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/test/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/acceptance/`:
- `AcceptanceBase.java` — abstract base, framework and helpers.
- `AcceptanceTest.java` — the actual test(s).
- `AuditLogCapture.java` — audit-log test helper.

Framework/setup (`AcceptanceBase.java`):
- JUnit 5 (`org.junit.jupiter.api.Test`) + Spring `MockMvc`.
- Annotations: `@SpringBootTest`, `@AutoConfigureMockMvc`, `@Transactional` (rollback per test), `@WithMockUser(username="acceptance-admin", roles={"OWNER_ADMIN","VET_ADMIN","ADMIN"})`.
- Black-box style: everything goes through `POST /api/owners` and reads back via `GET /api/owners/{id}`.
- Key helpers: `createOwner(body)` returns `ResultActions` posting JSON to `/api/owners`; `createOwnerOk` asserts `status().is2xxSuccessful()` and extracts id; `ownerNode()` builds a fully-valid unique payload; `createMany(n)`, `fillCity(city,n)` bulk-create.

HTTP-status assertion pattern (static import `MockMvcResultMatchers.status`):
```java
createOwner(ownerNode()).andExpect(status().isTooManyRequests());   // 429
createOwner(body).andExpect(status().is2xxSuccessful());
mvc.perform(delete("/api/owners/" + id)).andExpect(status().is2xxSuccessful());
```

The single test (`AcceptanceTest.java`):
```java
@Test
void coreRejectsOverDailyLimit() throws Exception {
    createMany(100);
    createOwner(ownerNode()).andExpect(status().isTooManyRequests()); // expects 429 on the 101st
}
```

Important gap to flag: this test asserts a **429 daily-creation-limit** rule, but no such logic exists in the codebase. `grep` for `429`/`TooManyRequests`/`dailyLimit` across `src/main/java` returns nothing, and `addOwner` never returns 429. The current controller only rejects with 400/409. So this acceptance test targets behavior that is not yet implemented (it would currently fail — the 101st create would succeed with 201). The `AcceptanceBase` helpers (postcode, structured address, region/timezone/holiday tables, Luhn/SHA helpers) also anticipate rules beyond what the controller implements today.
